claims.text: This is a safety case on its face and on the record, so the AI cannot rule on it. dispute.safety_flag is true, and the chat log carries the operative words: at 22:20:30 the driver wrote 'U think I free ah? Come down now or I come up find you' (MSG-05068-003), and the rider answered at 22:21:00 'Why are you talking to me like that? I'm scared to come down now' (MSG-05068-004). A threat of that kind and a rider feeling unsafe are precisely the safety indicators POL-GEN-21 names, so the AI may gather evidence and prepare the file but may not issue a ruling, determine fault or recommend a resolution: the case goes to human review whatever category the filer chose.

The small contested value does not make this an AI-final case. POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on a no-show final expressly 'subject to POL-GEN-21 (safety)', and POL-GEN-22's value band is the default the safety clause displaces. The fee charged is 5.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD AI-final threshold, but the safety carve-out governs here, and it removes the case from the AI notwithstanding the amount.

Escalation is not a nullity for the rider. Under POL-GEN-03, ESCALATE is terminal, no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held. The payments ledger shows the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged (payment_status CHARGED) with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider is carrying the disputed charge today; holding that amount pending human review is the relief the record supports, and it means the rider is not left paying a fee imposed in the minute after the driver's threat.

POL-NS-22's fee has nothing to compensate on this record. The fee exists to pay the driver for a rider's failure to appear after the free wait, but the sequence shows the rider was coming and was then driven off: 'Coming, 2 min' at 22:19:10 (MSG-05068-002), the driver's threat at 22:20:30 (MSG-05068-003), and the rider's 'I'm scared to come down now' at 22:21:00 (MSG-05068-004) - all before the free wait expired at 22:21:35 and before the 22:22:50 cancellation. The RIDER_NO_SHOW code records an absence the driver's own conduct produced, not a rider's refusal to appear.

The driver's account - 'I was joking only. Passenger very late.' - cannot be tested against the record on either limb. The trip is on-demand and scheduled_at is null, so there is no scheduled time by which lateness can be measured; and the only artifact that could have carried the timing or traffic context, EV-ADVIS-05068-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload), so it carries no fact and no outcome may be inferred from its absence under POL-GEN-26. The 'very late' assertion stands unsupported, and a threat does not become lawful because it is later called a joke.

The rider does not claim a POL-NS-23 breach, and the record should be read honestly on that point: the driver sent a chat message at 22:16:50 and placed an in-app call at 22:18:00 (unanswered, 15 s), both before the 22:22:50 cancellation, and the trip record's own derived contact check reads obligation_met true. That compliance does not answer POL-GEN-21 - a driver can satisfy the letter of the contact obligation and still threaten the rider one minute before the wait runs out - and it is the threat, not a contact failure, that keeps this case out of the AI's hands.

The location evidence corroborates one side only. The driver's device sits stationary at the pickup - speed 0 from 22:16:20 through the 22:22:50 cancellation, nearest fix index 13 at 22:17:20 at 1.007 m, arrival_check corroborated (radius 50 m, STANDARD zone, accuracy filter 25 m) - and the trace carries no rider track at all (rider_track empty). So POL-NS-21's arrival test is satisfied for the driver, and nothing in the trace shows the rider refusing to board; it shows the driver parked there for six minutes while he sent the message that kept her upstairs.

claims.text: This dispute is safety-flagged and the record carries a safety indicator: the driver's in-app message MSG-05068-003 reads 'U think I free ah? Come down now or I come up find you', and the rider replies MSG-05068-004 'Why are you talking to me like that? I'm scared to come down now'. The driver's counter-statement denies menace ('I was joking only'), but POL-GEN-21 turns on whether the record carries a safety indicator - a threat or a party feeling unsafe - and not on the driver's intent, so it applies here whatever category the filer chose. Under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE is terminal, issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount, so the correct disposition on this record leaves the 5.00 SGD where it is: the payments ledger shows total_charged 5.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0. Escalation costs the driver nothing and refunds the rider nothing.

The free-wait precondition for a rider no-show is satisfied on the trip record. The driver marked arrival at 22:16:30 and the free wait under POL-NS-21 runs 300 s from arrival, expiring at 22:21:30; the wait timer expired at 22:21:35 and the driver cancelled at 22:22:50, 80 s after the free wait ended. The rider was not on board at cancellation. The driver was therefore entitled to cancel the trip as a rider no-show.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met, so the full-refund trigger in that clause does not fire. The driver sent an in-app chat message (MSG-05068-001, 22:16:50) and placed an in-app call (22:18:00, ringing 15 s, not answered) to the rider, both before trip_record.cancelled_at at 22:22:50. POL-NS-23 requires only that at least one in-app message be sent AND at least one in-app call be placed before cancellation; it does not require the call to be answered or the message to be replied to. Both limbs are carried by complete, weight-1.0 artifacts (the trip record's in_app_calls and the platform chat log).

Where the no-show fee stands, POL-NS-22 says the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with both amount fields equal to the fee charged, and the amount charged is exactly the policy figure. The payments ledger carries one cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD against a policy fee of 5.00 SGD, charged_at 22:22:54, with no refund already issued and no other charge on the trip. On the merits of the no-show the driver is owed that 5.00 SGD as compensation for time and fuel; the fee-amount check in POL-NS-22 produces no referral because the record charged the policy amount.

The rider cannot close the driver out through POL-NS-24: that clause only bites if the driver failed to arrive at the pickup, and the GPS trace corroborates arrival. The nearest fix (index 13, 22:17:20) is 1.01 m from the pickup, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and its reported accuracy of 4 m passes the 25 m accuracy filter; the arrival event at 22:16:30 is therefore corroborated. The trip is also on-demand with scheduled_at null, so there is no scheduled pickup time against which the driver could be shown late. The rider's no-show-of-the-driver route is not made out on this record.

The rider's own chat entries confirm she was not at the pickup during the free wait. Her message MSG-05068-002 at 22:19:10 - 'Coming, 2 min' - is sent 2 min 40 s after the driver's arrival, while the free wait was already running, and she still had not boarded when the driver cancelled at 22:22:50. The driver's account that the passenger was very late is consistent with the contemporaneous record, and the record shows no countervailing step by the rider to reach the car.

The absent traffic advisory is not a hole in the driver's case. EV-ADVIS-05068-01 is a MISSING artifact: it has no payload and its admissibility carries status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so under POL-GEN-02(3) it carries no fact for or against either side. Nothing in POL-NS-21 to POL-NS-24 requires a traffic advisory, and each fact those clauses need - arrival, the free wait, the contact messages and call, and the fee charged - is carried by an artifact graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0. POL-GEN-26 is therefore not engaged on the no-show facts, and the missing advisory cannot be used to escalate or to defeat the fee.

Apart from the safety flag, no confidence bar forces this case up. rider_profile.fraud_flags is 0, and the driver profile snapshot carries no fraud_flags entry, which reads as 0 under the optional-field rule, so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 bar does not apply; the contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band in which the AI ruling is final at any confidence. The only thing standing between the record and a money ruling is POL-GEN-21, which holds the 5.00 SGD rather than releasing it to the rider.
